title: The Rooftop Garden
summary: A tenant who wants to build a garden on a shared roof discovers that persuading her neighbours is harder than growing tomatoes.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: a woman watering plants in wooden boxes on a city rooftop at sunset, neighbours chatting nearby, no text

chapters.title: An Empty Roof
sentences: Mia had lived in the same apartment building for three years, and she had never spoken to most of her neighbours.
One Saturday she climbed the stairs to the roof and found a large, empty space covered with dust.
She imagined wooden boxes full of tomatoes, herbs and flowers, and the idea immediately excited her.
However, the roof belonged to everybody, so she needed permission from the residents.
She wrote a polite note and pinned it on the notice board in the entrance hall.
A week later she had received only one reply, and it was a refusal.
The neighbour on the third floor worried that the weight of the soil might damage the ceiling.
Mia felt disappointed, but she decided that the objection was reasonable and deserved a proper answer.

chapters.title: Doing Her Homework
sentences: Mia spent the next weekend learning about roof gardens and how to build them safely.
She discovered that light plastic containers filled with special lightweight soil weigh much less than people expect.
She also asked an engineer from her office to examine the roof and write a short report.
The engineer confirmed that the structure could easily support the extra weight if the boxes were spread out.
Mia printed the report and invited everyone to a meeting in the entrance hall.
Only seven people came, and several of them looked doubtful at first.
Calmly, she presented the plan, showed them the report and promised to pay for all the equipment.
Then she offered each family a box of their own, free of charge.
By the end of the evening, the third-floor neighbour had become her first volunteer.

chapters.title: The First Harvest
sentences: By midsummer, before the first harvest, the roof looked completely different, with green leaves and red tomatoes growing in neat rows.
Mia had expected a quiet hobby, but the garden quickly became the centre of the building.
Neighbours who used to nod politely now stopped to exchange advice about water and sunlight.
An elderly man taught the children how to plant beans, and in return they carried his shopping upstairs.
One evening the residents arranged a small dinner using vegetables from the roof.
Mia sat at the long table and realised that she knew everyone's name.
She had started the project because she wanted fresh tomatoes, but she had gained something far more valuable.
The building was no longer a collection of separate doors; it had become a community.
